pains.title: No single set of financials for the whole group
pains.problem: Each location or acquired practice arrives with its own chart of accounts and banks. Spreadsheet consolidation becomes a monthly project.
pains.how: Lucid delivers consolidated financials with a live group dashboard, and reports each entity on its own. Most practices are live in about 24 hours.

pains.title: Management fees and intercompany balances never match
pains.problem: The professional corporation pays the management company a fee, and shared costs and loans create balances that must match on both sides.
pains.how: Lucid books the fee as your management agreement says and checks both sides every month. Your attorney sets the fee terms, and Lucid keeps the numbers tied out.

pains.title: You cannot tell which location makes money
pains.problem: A consolidated statement averages a strong site with a weak one, and shared costs have no natural home.
pains.how: Lucid reports live profit and loss and margin by location, plus cost and margin by provider. Lucid does not run billing or chase claims.

faq.q: How do I get one set of financials for my group with several locations?
faq.a: Each entity keeps its own books, and Lucid combines them into one consolidated report each month. You also get each entity and each location on its own. You see the whole group and every site side by side.

faq.q: How do I account for management fees between my PC and my MSO?
faq.a: The fee is booked as income in the management company and an expense in the professional corporation, following your management agreement. Both sides should match every month and cancel out on the consolidated report. Lucid handles the intercompany reconciliation. Your healthcare attorney sets the fee terms.

faq.q: How do I know which of my locations is actually making money?
faq.a: Revenue and costs are coded to each location all year. Lucid gives you live profit and loss and margin by location or provider, so you see each site on its own.

faq.q: How do I get my group's books ready for a private equity buyer?
faq.a: Buyers want clean monthly statements for each entity and for the group, owner expenses kept separate and one time costs documented. Lucid cleans up and standardizes your books now so a buyer's review finds fewer surprises. Start early, since cleanup takes time. Lucid does not run the deal or value the group.

faq.q: Do I need separate tax returns for each entity?
faq.a: Usually yes for corporations and partnerships. A single member LLC that is disregarded for tax is reported on its owner's return. Your CPA confirms how each entity is treated, and your attorney confirms the legal structure.
